title: What the Fig Tree Withheld for Seven Years
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] My grandfather planted a fig tree the year I was born, a gesture I understood, for most of my childhood, as merely sentimental rather than instructive.
Narrator: For seven consecutive years, that tree produced nothing worth mentioning, a handful of shriveled, inedible fruit that fell before ripening and rotted quietly in the grass.
Narrator: [carefully] My grandfather never once proposed uprooting it, despite my father's periodic suggestion that the space might be better allocated to something more obliging.
Narrator: He simply kept tending it, pruning with an almost liturgical patience, as though barrenness were a phase to be outlasted rather than a verdict to be accepted.
Narrator: [reflective] I asked him once, with the impatience peculiar to adolescence, why he bothered persisting with something so stubbornly unproductive.

Narrator: He told me that a tree owes nothing to a calendar, that fruitfulness arrives on a timeline utterly indifferent to our impatience, and that uprooting it prematurely would only guarantee the harvest never came.
Narrator: [honestly] I didn't fully register the weight of that answer then, filed it away as one of his characteristically cryptic pronouncements, and largely forgot it.
Narrator: The eighth summer, inexplicably, the tree surrendered an abundance so sudden it seemed almost to mock the years of apparent failure preceding it.

Narrator: [gently] Watching him gather that first proper harvest, I understood, belatedly, that he'd never actually been waiting on the tree at all. He'd been demonstrating something considerably larger about patience itself.
Narrator: I think of that fig tree often now, whenever some effort of mine yields nothing for longer than seems reasonable, whenever I'm tempted toward the premature verdict that barrenness is final.
Narrator: [calmly] My grandfather has been gone a decade, but that tree still bears fruit every summer, and every summer I remember precisely what it was actually teaching me all along.

The tree produced the same small amount as before
The family finally uprooted it
The tree surrendered an abundance so sudden it seemed to mock the years of apparent failure
quiz.explanation: In the eighth summer, the tree inexplicably produced an abundance so sudden it seemed to mock the prior years of failure.
